Return available authentication methods.

post.description:
Authenticate using Plex token.

Args:
    request: Plex authentication request with authToken.

Returns:
    TokenResponse with JWT access token and role.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 if Plex auth is disabled.
    HTTPException: 401 if Plex token is invalid.
    HTTPException: 403 if user lacks access to configured server.
    HTTPException: 503 if plex.tv is unreachable or misbehaving.

Swap a valid session token for a fresh one with the same sign-in time.

An expired token cannot refresh, and no token refreshes more than
SESSION_MAX_AGE_DAYS after the original sign-in. The role is re-derived,
so a demoted admin comes back as a viewer.

Args:
    current_user: The verified token being refreshed.

Returns:
    TokenResponse with the new access token and role.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 401 if the session is past its cap or the user no
        longer has a way to sign in.
    HTTPException: 503 if plex.tv can't confirm an admin Plex token's role.

Authenticate user and return JWT token.

Args:

Returns:
    TokenResponse with access token and role.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 if local auth is disabled.
    HTTPException: 401 if credentials are invalid.

get.description:
Check if cast feature is enabled.

This endpoint allows the frontend to conditionally show/hide
the cast button based on the server-side feature flag.

Serve HLS playlist or segment files.

This endpoint is called by the Chromecast device to fetch the HLS stream.
No auth required - the session_id UUID acts as authentication since it's
hard to guess and sessions are time-limited. This is necessary because
Chromecast fetches segments via relative URLs without query params.

post.description:
Create a new cast session.

For HLS streams (ErsatzTV): returns an ErsatzTV stream session's playlist
path, with no transcoding and no cast session.
For MPEG-TS streams: Starts FFmpeg transcoding and returns HLS URL.

get.description:
Get the currently airing program for every channel.

Requires JWT authentication. Lets a channel list show what is on each
channel without one request per channel.

The grouped channel catalogue (the list the channel picker shows) is
resolved by guide id with the same display-name fallback as the single
lookup. When the catalogue is unavailable, only XMLTV ids are returned.

Args:
    current_user: Authenticated user from JWT token.

Returns:
    NowPlayingBulkResponse mapping channel id to its current program.
    Channels with nothing on air are omitted.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 503 if EPG service is unavailable.

Get a channel's schedule from the XMLTV guide.

Requires JWT authentication. Returns the programmes that end after
30 minutes ago and start within the next `hours` hours, in start order.

Args:
    channel_id: Guide id of the channel to look up.
    hours: How many hours ahead of now to include (1-48).
    channel_name: Optional channel name to fall back on.
    current_user: Authenticated user from JWT token.

Returns:
    EPGProgrammesResponse with the channel's programmes in the window.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 503 if EPG service is unavailable.

get.description:
Coarse upstream readiness for the uptime monitor, from local state only.

Public, so it carries no URLs, error text or counts, and it never waits on
an upstream. When the guide or the Dispatcharr catalogue is due and not
backing off it starts one background refresh of it (at most one per TTL or
backoff window), so on an idle app 'stale' and 'failing' mean the refresh
is failing, not that nobody asked. The Docker healthcheck stays on
/api/health: an upstream outage must not get this container restarted.

schema.title: Response Health Deps Api Health Deps Get
